title: Physiological responses to a 6-d taper in middle-distance runners: influence of training intensity and volume
authors: Mujika I, Goya A, Padilla S, Grijalba A, Gorostiaga E, Ibanez J
journal: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
population: Well-trained male middle-distance runners after 15 weeks of training
findings: 8 runners were randomly assigned to a moderate volume taper (50% progressive reduction, n=4) or a low volume taper (75% progressive reduction, n=4) of low intensity continuous and high intensity interval training.
800 m performance was not significantly enhanced by either taper (LVT 124.9 +/- 4.5 vs 126.1 +/- 4.2 s; MVT 126.2 +/- 8.0 vs 125.7 +/- 6.6 s).

Red cell count, haemoglobin, mean corpuscular volume and mean corpuscular Hb concentration significantly decreased with taper while reticulocyte count increased; physiological changes were mainly haematological.

Performance changes correlated with changes in postrace peak blood lactate (r = 0.87, P < 0.01); authors conclude middle-distance runners can progressively reduce usual training volume by at least 75% during a 6-d taper.
limitations: n=8 total (underpowered), no non-taper control group, 800 m runners, 6-day taper; absence of a significant improvement is not evidence of no effect.
implications: A very short taper should be presented as freshness preparation, not a promised improvement.
Performance was not reduced by cutting volume 50-75% over 6 days in this small sample, so the lower bound of the volume band is not alarming, but there was no control group to confirm this.
No change to the 14-day, 41-60% default is justified by this study.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (MSSE Feb 2000; Crossref author field shows a mangled 'Ibanez'). 'Randomly assigned' stated in abstract so rct label kept.
